title: Researching How We Learn
summary: A 70-minute inquiry. If attendance weren't the organising principle of education, how would you learn? Alpha School's AI-driven 'two-hour school day' is the case study.
overview: Frame: each student picks one real thing they want to get better at (maths, an essay, a language, exam prep) as their test case. They then look at Alpha School's claims (2 hours a day, 2.3× growth) next to coverage from Scientific American and WIRED.

Investigate: students listen to 20 minutes of a Huberman Lab podcast with Alpha co-founder Joe Liemandt, treating him as a source who knows the model well and also has a stake in its success. Prompts separate claim, evidence, cause and transfer, and an optional sports-training analogy lets them see where the comparison breaks down.

Develop: students sketch their own learning loop (attempt, feedback, adjustment, retention test) on a built-in drawing canvas, then save it as an image or PDF. Work is saved in the browser as they go.
questions: What would distinguish real learning from short-term performance?
How far should we trust claims from people with a stake in the outcome?
Can a method that works in one context transfer to another?
